Hi Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can map to the right commercial path: 

Summary from our side:
- Objective: 6-week pilot to validate latency and integration with Clearway's EHR routing (expected ~2M tokens).
- Target start: early July.
- Expected spend: ~$45k - $90k for the pilot depending on usage spikes.

Procurement items we need to confirm: 
1) You mentioned the county/state policy prevents issuing a PO for pilots and that Clearway prefers using a corporate PCard or prepay via vendor portal. Can you confirm whether a single PCard transaction up to $75k is acceptable, or if multiple transactions are required?
2) If PCard is not feasible, would Clearway consider a prepay invoice for the pilot amount? If prepay is required, what approval lead time should we expect?
3) Is there interest in purchasing via AWS/Azure marketplace (you mentioned exploring marketplace options)? If so, we can share our marketplace listing notes and timeline.

I've attached a brief pricing preview and our standard SOW for pilots to help procurement review. If a PO is absolutely not possible, we may need a one-off commercial exception (card-only pilot or short prepay invoice). If that is the case, please let us know who in procurement/finance needs to sign off so we can route properly.

Next steps I propose: 
- Alicia: confirm whether PCard single-transaction up to $75k is allowed, or if multiple card transactions are necessary.
- Daniel: if vendor portal/prepay is preferred, please share the procurement intake link and timeline.
- Camila/Redwood: prep an exception request template and a narrowed invoice amount once you confirm the numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Correct: for pilots under our current state-contracted policy we are not able to issue a standard PO to vendors for pilot engagements unless the vendor is already on contract. That rules out our normal PO flow for this pilot.
- Short-term options we can use: (a) Corporate PCard (we have a single card limit of $75k per transaction); (b) Vendor prepay via our vendor portal (must be routed through Finance and requires payment on approval — lead time ~7-10 business days once finance has an approved invoice); or (c) Marketplace procurement (preferred if the vendor is listed; marketplace purchases follow a separate procurement flow and are generally faster).
- For amounts above $75k we would need to either split the charge across multiple card transactions (requires manager approval in advance) or approve a one-time exception via our procurement director (exception route takes ~2 weeks to approve).

Given the pilot estimate you shared (~$45k-$90k), it sounds like we may need to either: 1) do a single PCard up to $75k and then top up with a second card txn if needed, or 2) go the prepay route if you can provide an invoice early. 

I can introduce you to our procurement manager (cc'd procurement-team) if you'd like to request a formal exception. We also prefer marketplace purchases where possible — I will check whether Clearway's marketplace team can approve Redwood for the procurement window you need.

Regards,
Alicia Torres
Procurement Lead | Clearway Health
alicia.torres@clearwayhealth.com

Option B — Prepay invoice: Redwood issues an invoice for the expected pilot amount; Clearway pays via vendor portal. Prepay lead time ~7-10 business days, which could push schedule if approvals are slow.

Option C — Marketplace purchase: If Redwood is available on the marketplace and can get approved, procurement prefers this path. Time to enable depends on our marketplace listing status.
